_comment: WC2026 THIRD-PLACE MATCH (M103, 2026-07-18): France (SF loser to Spain) vs England (SF loser to Argentina). MEASURED PROFILES (8 matches each): FRANCE (rating 94) -- GF 16 / GA 5; three straight knockout clean sheets (Sweden, Paraguay, Morocco) before Spain blanked them 2-0 in the semi; the classiest side not in the final. ENGLAND (rating 91) -- GF 14 / GA 8; scored in SEVEN of eight (all but the 0-0 vs Ghana), BTTS-Yes in six of eight, leaky back, open games throughout. THIRD-PLACE CONTEXT (texture modifier): historically the most OPEN game of a tournament -- little at stake, rotations, loose legs -> goals up, caution down; this pushes Over/BTTS higher than a semi between the same sides and softens France's defensive edge. Class gap ~3 -> France the moderate favourite (better side, better tournament defence), England's ever-present attack keeps BTTS live. A/B PROTOCOL: PASS A (blind, estimation-only) issued first -- lambdas FRA 1.55 / ENG 1.15 -> France 45.7 / Draw 26.9 / England 27.4; advancement France 60.4 / England 39.6; total 2.70, Over 2.5 a coin-flip (50.6%), BTTS-Yes 54.7%. PASS B (real Bet365 board) PENDING -- the market row below is an ESTIMATE until the user supplies the live line; the bottom line is provisional (model-only) and will be re-issued/confirmed on the real board per the standing real-odds rule. Home = France (nominal; neutral venue). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.grade: ❌ MISS on the side -- the committed pick (France) lost; England won from the 27.4% branch. The committed MARKETS both landed emphatically: Over 2.5 ✅ (10 goals vs the 2.5 line) and BTTS-Yes ✅ (4 and 6) -- the 'open, both-score third-place game' texture was directionally exact. The manner (90') also held. But side + scoreline (2-1 vs 4-6) miss, so ❌ under the strict rubric.
_postmatch.verdict: The texture thesis was right and radically UNDER-SCALED. I applied a third-place openness modifier (lifted totals to 2.70, softened France's defence to 0.95) and flagged rotations as the swing risk -- reality delivered the extreme version: total goals 10, a >4x overshoot of the expected total, presumably heavy rotations on both sides and zero defensive intensity. Honest note: NO Poisson-family model assigns meaningful mass to a 4-6 (it is a many-sigma tail on any calibration) -- the miss to own is not 'failed to predict 10 goals' but the SIDE: I gave France the class edge and their (rotated) defence collapsed harder than England's; England's attack -- the single most reliable scoring habit of the tournament (now scored in 8 of 9, and 6 in one game) -- out-gunned them. Also for the record: Pass B never happened (no live board supplied), so the call stayed model-only and flagged weaker, exactly as the real-odds rule prescribes.
_postmatch.lesson: Third-place games break MODELS, not just forecasts: with stakes near zero, defensive intensity -- the very thing every calibration is built on -- evaporates, and totals can land anywhere; treat third-place fixtures as the highest-variance match type in football and say so in the confidence note (cap confidence at LOW regardless of the class gap). The direction of the openness modifier is validated (Over/BTTS both landed) -- next time scale it HARDER and trust the class gap LESS (rotation quality is unknowable pre-match). England close their tournament having scored in 8 of 9 games; Kane's side leaves with the bronze. One match left: the FINAL, Spain-Argentina.
